title: Seven metrics give complementary views of performance
alt: Five-model, seven-metric scorecard with numeric cell labels. Majority-baseline precision is gray and explicitly undefined.
interpretation: Read a column down to compare models on that metric. Values across unlike metrics are not a composite ranking.

title: False negatives outnumber false positives in every model
alt: Two zero-based count panels show false positives and false negatives for all five models, including the zero-positive majority baseline.
interpretation: Compare error types within a model, then compare models on the common count scale. Different actual-class sizes prevent reading counts as rates.

title: Every trained model improves on the majority baseline
alt: Separate panels compare accuracy gain in percentage points and relative error reduction in percent against the majority baseline.
interpretation: The left panel measures absolute accuracy improvement; the right panel measures the fraction of baseline mistakes avoided. Units differ.

title: Precision and recall describe the saved decisions
alt: Four trained models appear as individually labeled precision-recall points at their saved thresholds. Undefined baseline precision is stated below.
interpretation: Higher precision and recall describe this fixed decision rule. The chart does not tune thresholds or establish a superior threshold policy.

title: Probability quality improves beyond the constant baseline
alt: Two zero-based bar panels compare Brier score and log loss for the four models with probability outputs; SVM is explicitly excluded.
interpretation: Lower values are better within each score. Probability quality includes both calibration and discrimination; clipping affects log loss.

title: Calibration gaps show overprediction and underprediction
alt: Four faceted signed calibration-gap plots show occupied bins, sample-sized points, transformed Wilson intervals, and a zero-reference line.
interpretation: Positive gaps indicate overprediction and negative gaps underprediction. Large intervals signal sparse bins; a constant baseline can match prevalence.

title: All 13 trained configurations in the validation search
alt: Four model-family panels show all 13 trained configurations, five fold scores per configuration, their means, and explicit selected labels.
interpretation: Selected means maximize the declared training-CV selection metric within each family. Fold spread is descriptive and selection-biased, not a confidence interval.

title: Random forest errors vary across historical groups
alt: Seven recorded sex and race groups have random-forest recall and false-positive-rate estimates, Wilson intervals, and metric-specific denominators.
interpretation: Group estimates describe this historical sample. Inspect interval width and positive/negative denominators before comparing rates; this is not fairness certification.

title: Test results differ between seen and novel model profiles
alt: Balanced accuracy and recall are compared for seen and novel model-input profiles across all five models, with both subset sample sizes stated.
interpretation: The profile subsets differ in case mix and prevalence. Their differences do not isolate causality or show that matching records are the same people.

title: Sample retention and class balance define the denominators
alt: Four zero-based panels show raw and retained training/test counts and the two income-class counts within each retained partition.
interpretation: Each retention share is relative to raw rows, while class shares are relative to retained rows. Counts across these panels should not be summed.
